## Natural history notes

A large foliose lichen characterized by broad pale gray to gray-green ruffled lobes, black-edged margins with small cilia, and distinctive perforations or holes in the reproductive structures. In Florida, the Perforated Ruffle Lichen grows on tree bark and branches in humid forests, hammocks, swamp edges, parks, and shaded yards where moisture and clean air support lichen growth. Like other lichens, it is a symbiosis between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner, absorbing moisture and nutrients from the air while adding texture to bark surfaces and providing tiny shelter for small invertebrates.
